sections.title: Your Day
sections.content: A routine needs two things: the verb, which you now know how to build, and a word saying when. Spanish puts the when either at the front or at the end, whichever you prefer — 'por la mañana trabajo' and 'trabajo por la mañana' are both good. Note that it is 'por la mañana', with the article, where English just says 'in the morning'.

items.spanish: Me levanto a las seis y media.
items.english: I get up at half past six.

items.spanish: A veces estudio solo y otras veces estudio con Meg.
items.english: Sometimes I study alone and other times I study with Meg.

items.spanish: Cada día leo un poco en español.
items.english: Each day I read a little in Spanish.

sections.content: Treat 'me levanto' as one phrase for now — that little 'me' belongs to a family of verbs you turn back on yourself, and they get a lesson of their own later. For the moment: 'me levanto' for I get up, 'se levanta' for he or she gets up.

sections.topic: the reflexive verbs that 'me levanto' belongs to
